right-sws-schema-edit:
{{doc-right|sws-schema-edit}}
Name of the user right required to create and edit pages in the SWS Schema namespace.
right-sws-layout-edit:
{{doc-right|sws-layout-edit}}
Name of the user right required to create and edit pages in the SWS Layout namespace.
right-sws-mapping-edit:
{{doc-right|sws-mapping-edit}}
Name of the user right required to create and edit pages in the SWS Mapping namespace.
right-sws-query:
{{doc-right|sws-query}}
Name of the user right required to run SWS queries, such as via the Cypher query API.
right-sws-admin:
{{doc-right|sws-admin}}
Name of the user right required to report and rebuild the wiki's graph stores.
specialpages-group-sws: Group heading for SWS special pages on [[Special:SpecialPages]].
sws-special-subjects:
{{doc-special|Subjects}}
Title of [[Special:Subjects]], which lists every subject on the wiki. Also the caption of the subjects table on that page and on schema pages.
sws-subjects-column-subject:
Header of the column naming each subject in the subject tables on [[Special:Subjects]], schema pages and [[Special:SWS]].
{{Identical|Subject}}
sws-subjects-column-schema: Header of the column naming each subject's schema in the subject tables.
sws-subjects-column-page:
Header of the column naming the page that holds each subject in the subject tables.
{{Identical|Page}}
sws-subjects-column-edited: Header of the column showing when each subject was last edited.
sws-subjects-empty: Shown in a subject table when the wiki has no subjects.
sws-subjects-empty-schema:
Shown in a subject table, and on a Schema card on [[Special:Schemas]], when a schema has no subjects.

Parameters:
* $1 - the schema name
sws-subjects-no-match:
Shown in a subject table when no subject matches the search.

Parameters:
* $1 - the search text
sws-subjects-all-schemas: Item of the schema menu above the subject table on [[Special:Subjects]]; choosing it shows the subjects of every schema.
sws-subjects-schema-label:
Accessible name of the schema menu above the subject table on [[Special:Subjects]].
{{Identical|Schema}}
sws-subjects-search-placeholder: Placeholder and accessible name of the search field of the subject tables, which matches subject labels, page titles and the start of subject IDs.
sws-subjects-load-error: Shown in a subject table in place of its rows, and on a Schema card on [[Special:Schemas]] in place of its subjects, when they could not be loaded.
sws-subjects-search-timeout: Shown in the subject table on [[Special:Subjects]] in place of its rows when a search across every schema ran past the time the wiki allows. Choosing a schema in the menu above the table searches fewer subjects.
sws-subjects-search-timeout-schema: Shown in a subject table in place of its rows when a search within one schema ran past the time the wiki allows.
sws-subjects-recently-edited: Caption of the [[Special:SWS]] table of the five most recently edited subjects. Adding a subject counts as editing it.
sws-subjects-view-all: Link to [[Special:Subjects]]: from the table of the recently edited subjects on [[Special:SWS]], and from each Schema card and table row on [[Special:Schemas]] to that schema's subjects, replacing {{msg-mw|sws-schema-subject-count}} for readers who see no counts.
sws-overview-subjects-description: Description of the card on [[Special:SWS]] that leads to [[Special:Subjects]].
sws-special-schemas: Title and description of the [[Special:Schemas]] page. Also the caption of the Schema table on that page and the title of its card on [[Special:SWS]].
sws-special-createsubject: Title and description of the [[Special:CreateSubject]] page, which creates a page together with its Main Subject. A subpage names the Schema to use, e.g. Special:CreateSubject/Person.
sws-schema-label: Names a subject's schema. $1 is the schema name or a link to it. Also used as the accessible name of the schema badge, whose visible text is the bare name.
sws-cypher-raw-error-json-encode: Error message shown when JSON encoding of query results fails.
sws-cypher-raw-error-not-configured: Error shown on the {{#cypher_raw}} parser function when the wiki has no Neo4j database configured.
sws-cypher-error-permission-denied: Error shown on the {{#cypher_raw}} parser function when the user the page is parsed for lacks the sws-query right.
sws-cypher-error-empty-query: Error shown on the {{#cypher_raw}} parser function and the nw.query() Lua function when the supplied Cypher query is empty or only whitespace.
sws-cypher-error-write-query: Error shown on the {{#cypher_raw}} parser function and the nw.query() Lua function when the query contains a write operation. Cypher queries from wikitext are restricted to read-only.
sws-cypher-error-syntax: Error shown when Neo4j reports a syntax error for a Cypher query run from wikitext. $1 is the verbatim Neo4j-supplied syntax detail and is not translatable.
sws-cypher-error-parameter-missing: Error shown when a Cypher query run from wikitext references a parameter that was not supplied. $1 is the verbatim Neo4j-supplied detail and is not translatable.
sws-cypher-error-timeout: Error shown when a Cypher query run from wikitext exceeds the allowed time limit. $1 is the verbatim Neo4j-supplied detail and is not translatable.
sws-cypher-error-backend-unavailable: Error shown when the graph database backend cannot be reached for a Cypher query run from wikitext. The underlying connection detail is intentionally omitted.
sws-cypher-error-internal: Generic fallback error shown for a Cypher query run from wikitext that fails for a reason not covered by the more specific cases. $1 is the verbatim underlying detail and is not translatable.
sws-sparql-raw-error-json-encode: Error message shown when JSON encoding of SPARQL query results fails.
sws-sparql-raw-error-not-configured: Error shown on the {{#sparql_raw}} parser function when the wiki has no SPARQL store configured.
sws-sparql-error-permission-denied: Error shown on the {{#sparql_raw}} parser function when the user the page is parsed for lacks the sws-query right.
sws-sparql-error-empty-query: Error shown on the {{#sparql_raw}} parser function and the nw.sparqlQuery() Lua function when the supplied SPARQL query is empty or only whitespace.
sws-sparql-error-syntax: Error shown when the SPARQL store rejects a query run from wikitext (a 4xx response, most commonly a syntax error). $1 is the verbatim store-supplied detail and is not translatable.
sws-sparql-error-store-unavailable: Error shown when the SPARQL store cannot be reached for a query run from wikitext (a 5xx response or a transport error). The underlying connection detail is intentionally omitted.
sws-sparql-error-internal: Generic fallback error shown for a SPARQL query run from wikitext that fails for a reason not covered by the more specific cases. $1 is the verbatim underlying detail and is not translatable.
sws-view-error-extra-positional: Error shown when {{#view}} is called with more than one positional argument. $1 is the offending extra argument value.
sws-view-error-conflicting-subject: Error shown when {{#view}} receives a Subject ID as both a positional argument and a named subject= argument.
sws-view-error-unknown-arg: Error shown when {{#view}} receives an unrecognized named argument. $1 is the offending argument name.
sws-main-subject-error-argument:
Error shown where {{#main_subject}} stands when it is called with an argument. Parameters:
* $1 - the first argument given
sws-page-tools-label: Heading for the SWS section in the MediaWiki sidebar (shown as a group label in legacy skins and inside the page tools menu in modern Vector).
sws-page-tools-create-subject: Label for the link in the SWS section of the sidebar that opens the Subject creator on the page being viewed, with that page preselected. The dialog creates the page's Main Subject if it has none, or another Subject otherwise. Pages that cannot open the creator link to [[Special:CreateSubject]] instead, under {{msg-mw|sws-sidebar-create-subject}}, which reads the same.
sws-page-tools-edit-json: Label for the sidebar link that navigates to Special:NeoJson for the current page. Only visible when development UIs are enabled.
sws-page-tools-view-json: Read-only counterpart of sws-page-tools-edit-json: label for the sidebar link to Special:NeoJson, shown to users who lack edit permission. Only visible when development UIs are enabled.
sws-page-tools-rdf: Label for the sidebar link that opens the current page's RDF export (Turtle serialization of the page's Subjects), served by the per-page RDF REST endpoint. Shown on every existing content page.
sws-subject-creator-schema-field: Label of the field in the 'create subject' dialog that picks the Subject's schema. Not shown; read out by screen readers.
sws-subject-creator-no-schemas: Shown in the 'create subject' dialog in place of the schema field, on a wiki that has no schemas yet, to a user who may not create one.
sws-subject-creator-page-field: Label of the field group in the 'create subject' dialog that picks which page the Subject goes on.
sws-subject-creator-page-section: Title of the collapsible section of the 'create subject' dialog that holds the page choice, and, while it is collapsed, the choice made; it is also the header of the non-expandable block a {{#create_subject}} button shows when the page is fixed: {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-section-this}} and its siblings continue this title, so 'Store the subject on' plus 'this page' must read as one phrase.
sws-subject-creator-page-section-this: The choice shown in the header of the collapsed page section, continuing {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-section}}: the page the dialog was opened on. Lower case, as the end of that phrase.
sws-subject-creator-page-section-another: The choice shown in the header of the collapsed page section, continuing {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-section}}: a page that exists, none of which is picked yet, where the dialog was opened on a page of its own.
sws-subject-creator-page-section-existin: The choice shown in the header of the collapsed page section, continuing {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-section}}: a page that exists, none of which is picked yet, where the dialog was opened on no page of its own.
sws-subject-creator-page-section-picked:
The choice shown in the header of the collapsed page section, continuing {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-section}}: the page picked. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title
sws-subject-creator-page-section-new: The choice shown in the header of the collapsed page section, continuing {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-section}}: a page created for the Subject, with no title given for it. A {{#create_subject}} button with page=new also shows it in its non-expandable block, above a page-title field that may already be filled in.
sws-subject-creator-page-section-new-tit:
The choice shown in the header of the collapsed page section, continuing {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-section}}: a page created for the Subject under the title given. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title
sws-subject-creator-page-this: Label of the option that puts the Subject on the page the 'create subject' dialog was opened from.
sws-subject-creator-page-another: Label of the option that puts the Subject on an existing page the user picks in the 'create subject' dialog, where the dialog was opened on a page of its own. {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-existing}} names the same option where it was not.
sws-subject-creator-page-existing: Label of the option that puts the Subject on an existing page the user picks in the 'create subject' dialog, where the dialog was opened on no page of its own - Special:CreateSubject, a Schema page - so there is no page to call it another of. {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-another}} names the same option where there is.
sws-subject-creator-page-new: Label of the option that gives the Subject a page of its own, created together with it by the 'create subject' dialog.
sws-subject-creator-page-new-denied: Shown below the disabled {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-new}} option of the 'create subject' dialog, for a user without the right to create pages.
sws-subject-creator-page-picked:
Note in the 'create subject' dialog when the page picked has no Main Subject of its own. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title
sws-subject-creator-page-has-main-subjec:
Note in the 'create subject' dialog when the chosen page already has a Main Subject. Parameters:
* $1 - the display name of that Main Subject
sws-subject-creator-page-title-field: Label of the field in the 'create subject' dialog that titles the page created for the Subject.
sws-subject-creator-page-title-required: Error shown at the page-title field of the 'create subject' dialog when a new page is saved with the field empty.
sws-subject-creator-page-title-invalid:
Error shown at the page-title field of the 'create subject' dialog when the title given can title no page. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title given
sws-subject-creator-page-taken:
Error shown at the page-title field of the 'create subject' dialog, in its "Store the subject on" section or below the summary line of a new page a {{#create_subject}} button named, when the title chosen for the new page is already taken. See also {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-taken-retitle}}. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title
sws-subject-creator-page-taken-retitle:
Error shown at the page-title field below the summary line of a new page a {{#create_subject}} button asked for without naming it (page=new), when the title chosen is already taken: only the title can change there. See also {{msg-mw|sws-subject-creator-page-taken}}. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title
sws-subject-creator-page-read-error:
Error shown at the page field of the 'create subject' dialog when the chosen page's Subjects could not be read. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title
sws-subject-creator-id-in-use:
Error shown when the 'create subject' dialog, opened from a red link, could not create the subject the link points to, because the wiki already holds a subject with that ID. That subject may be on a page the user may not read, so the message must not say whether the user can see it or who created it. Parameters:
* $1 - the subject ID
sws-createsubject-button: Label of the button that opens the 'create subject' dialog: the main button on [[Special:SWS]], and the button on [[Special:CreateSubject]] that reopens the dialog after it was closed.
sws-schema-editor-summary-default: Default edit summary used when updating a schema via the UI.
sws-schema-editor-success: Success notification shown after updating a schema. $1 is the schema name.
sws-schema-editor-error: Error notification title shown when updating a schema fails. $1 is the schema name.
sws-schema-editor-new-property: Label for the button that adds a new property definition in the schema editor. Translations can only exceed the English length a little bit.
sws-schema-editor-new-property-shortcut: Tooltip of the button below the property list in the schema editor that adds a property definition. Ctrl+Enter, or Cmd+Enter on a Mac, does the same from anywhere in the schema editor; write the key names as they appear on keyboards in your language.
sws-schema-editor-delete-property: Aria label for the button that deletes a property definition in the schema editor.
sws-schema-editor-subject-label: Title of the fixed first row of the property list in the schema editor, and heading of the pane shown when that row is selected. The row stands for the optional label of a subject: its name or title. Use the term for a subject's label used in {{msg-mw|sws-subject-editor-label-field}}.
sws-schema-editor-subject-label-help: Text of the pane shown when the Label row of the schema editor's property list is selected. "Name" and "Title" are the names of properties a user might otherwise add for the label; translate them.
sws-schema-editor-description: Label for the description field in the schema editor.
sws-schema-editor-resize-property-list: Accessible name of the divider between the property list and the property editor in the schema editor. Dragging it, or moving it with the arrow keys, changes how wide the property list is.
sws-schema-editor-description-placeholde: Placeholder text for the description field in the schema editor.
sws-schema-editor-description-edit: Accessibility label and tooltip for the button that starts editing the schema description in the schema editor dialog header.
sws-schema-editor-description-expand: Accessibility label and tooltip for the button that expands a schema description truncated to two lines.
sws-schema-editor-description-collapse: Accessibility label and tooltip for the button that collapses an expanded schema description back to two lines.
sws-schema-editor-description-add: Label of the button that starts writing a description for a schema that has none, shown in the schema editor dialog header.
sws-schema-subjects-are-dependent: Shown read-only on the page of a schema that declares its subjects dependent, in the schema editor, and in the schema creator where this was decided for the user. That declaration is made when a schema is created and cannot be changed.
sws-schema-editor-no-properties-dependen: Text of the schema editor's property pane for a schema that declares its subjects dependent and has no property definitions yet. Such a schema has no Label row, since dependent subjects have no label.
sws-subject-generated-name: The name shown for a subject that has no label of its own and is not named after its page, so nobody chose its name. $1 is the subject's identifier, such as s1ab2cd3ef4gh5i. The round brackets mark the whole string as a stand-in the system supplied rather than a name someone typed, as in {{msg-mw|Blanknamespace}}; use whichever brackets your language uses for that.
sws-relation-target-not-found-title: Tooltip of the red link shown for a relation value whose target subject the wiki cannot show the reader, either because no subject has that ID or because it is on a page the reader may not read. $1 is the subject's identifier, such as s1ab2cd3ef4gh5i, which is also the link text. The counterpart of {{msg-mw|Red-link-title}}, but word it so it neither asserts the subject is absent nor mentions permissions: each would be wrong in one of the two cases.
sws-dependent-subject-name: The name of a dependent subject, which has no label of its own, such as "Birth of Pablo Picasso". $1 is the name of its schema, a word the wiki's own users chose. $2 is the name of its host subject: a name someone chose, its identifier in brackets ({{msg-mw|Sws-subject-generated-name}}) where nobody did, or a name composed with this message where the host subject is a dependent subject too, as in "Record of Birth of Pablo Picasso". Both are in an unknown language and grammatical gender, so do not inflect them, do not change their case, and make no word agree with them.
sws-dependent-subject-identified-name:
The name of a dependent subject where several named after the same host subject can be listed together, on the Data tab and in the delete confirmation, as in "Attendance of Rijksmuseum (Year: 2024)". Parameters:
* $1 - its name ({{msg-mw|sws-dependent-subject-name}})
* $2 - the name of the first property, in schema order, it holds a value for, a word the wiki's own users chose
* $3 - that value, as text
sws-search-hit-subject: Names the subject a search result matched, shown above the matching values. $1 is the subject's name and $2 the name of its schema: both are words the wiki's own users chose, in an unknown language and grammatical gender, so do not inflect them, do not change their case, and make no word agree with them. The round brackets set the schema name apart from the subject's name; use whichever brackets your language uses for that.
sws-search-hit-property-path: In a search result, joins the names of two properties: $1 that of a relation property, or two or more already joined this way, and $2 that of a property of the dependent subject it holds, as in "Birth › Place". Both are words the wiki's own users chose, so do not inflect them.
sws-subject-editor-title: Title of the subject editor dialog, and its accessible name. Names the task rather than a subject: the dialog can edit several at once, and each one is named by the pane that edits it.
sws-subject-editor-label: Label of the field in the subject creator and editor where a subject being created is given its label: its name or title. The interface adds "(optional)" after this text. Use the same word for "label" as in {{msg-mw|sws-subject-editor-label-field}}.
sws-subject-editor-label-field: Accessibility label for the input shown in place of the dialog title while renaming a subject in the subject editor dialog.
sws-subject-no-label: Stands in for a subject's label while the subject has none, unless the subject is shown under the name of its page. In the subject editor and creator, it is shown where the label of an existing subject goes, beside a button to set a label, and as the placeholder of the field that button opens. In the heading of the subject's page and of Special:Subject, the subject's identifier follows it in brackets.
sws-subject-editor-rename: Accessibility label for the button next to the subject editor dialog title that starts renaming the subject.
sws-subject-editor-open-target:
Label and tooltip of the control shown at the end of a relation field that is displaying its target, in the subject editor, which opens that subject for editing alongside the one being edited. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the subject it opens.
sws-subject-editor-summary-default: Default edit summary used when updating a subject via the UI.
sws-subject-editor-summary-default-creat: Default edit summary used when creating a subject via the UI.
sws-subject-editor-success: Success notification shown after updating a subject. $1 is the name the subject is shown under: a stored label, or the subject's bracketed identifier, such as "(s1ab2cd3ef4gh5i)", for a subject nobody named.
sws-subject-editor-success-multiple: Success notification shown after one save updated several subjects. $1 is how many.
sws-subject-editor-error: Error notification title shown when updating a subject fails. $1 is the name the subject is shown under: a stored label, or the subject's bracketed identifier, such as "(s1ab2cd3ef4gh5i)", for a subject nobody named.
sws-subject-editor-validation-failed: Toast title shown when the backend rejects a Subject save under enforcement. $1 is the name the subject is shown under: a stored label, or the subject's bracketed identifier, such as "(s1ab2cd3ef4gh5i)", for a subject nobody named. Keep the quotation marks around it, because a stored label is arbitrary text and needs delimiting.
sws-subject-editor-stored-on: Line in a subject editing pane on a page-first wiki saying which wiki page the subject is stored on. Parameters: $1 - the page name, which is rendered as a link to that page. The rest of the message is not part of the link.
sws-subject-editor-unsaved: Tooltip of the dot indicating a subject editing pane has unsaved changes.
sws-subject-editor-load-error: Error notification when the subject editor could not load what the form of the subject it was opened on needs, such as the dependent subjects edited inside it, or those a subject being created starts with. The editor closes again.
sws-subject-editor-loading: Accessible name of the progress bar the subject editor shows in place of its form while it reads what the form needs, once that takes a while.
sws-subject-editor-target-load-error: Error notification when a relation target subject could not be fetched for editing (missing, unreadable, or network failure).
sws-subject-editor-create-target-error: Error notification when a new subject could not be created from a relation field, because its schema or an identifier for it could not be fetched, or because no page could be determined to store it on.
sws-subject-editor-partial-save:
Message shown in the subject editor's footer when a multi-subject save wrote some subjects and then failed. Parameters:
* $1 - how many subjects were written, at least one
* $2 - how many the save attempted, at least two
sws-subject-editor-save-scope:
Note shown beside the subject editor's save button on a page-first wiki, naming what the save writes. Parameters:
* $1 - how many subjects the save writes
* $2 - how many wiki pages hold them
Shown only when the user cannot see the whole scope already, so $1 is at least two or the one changed subject is not the one on screen.
sws-subject-editor-save-scope-subject-fi:
Note shown beside the subject editor's save button on a subject-first wiki, naming how many subjects the save writes. Unlike {{msg-mw|sws-subject-editor-save-scope}}, it counts no pages. Parameters:
* $1 - how many subjects the save writes
Shown only when the user cannot see the whole scope already, so $1 is at least two or the one changed subject is not the one on screen.
sws-subject-editor-open-subjects: Accessible name of the list of subjects open in the subject editor, which the user selects one of to edit it. Shown only once a second subject has been opened.
sws-subject-editor-resize-navigator: Accessible name of the divider between the list of subjects and the edit form in the subject editor. Dragging it, or moving it with the arrow keys, changes how wide the list is. The list itself is named by {{msg-mw|sws-subject-editor-open-subjects}}.
sws-dependent-subject-add:
Label of the button below a relation field of the subject editor whose values are dependent subjects, which adds one; the field shows the fields of each dependent subject inline. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the schema of the dependent subject it adds.
sws-dependent-subject-add-choose: Label of the menu button below a relation field of the subject editor whose values are dependent subjects of several schemas. It opens a menu of those schemas, one of which the user picks to add a dependent subject of it.
sws-dependent-subject-remove:
Accessible name and tooltip of the button that removes one dependent subject from the relation field of the subject editor that shows it inline. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the dependent subject's group: its schema name, numbered where the field holds several of that schema ({{msg-mw|sws-dependent-subject-numbered}}).
sws-dependent-subject-removed:
Text of the card that takes the place of a dependent subject removed in the subject editor, with an {{msg-mw|sws-dependent-subject-undo}} button, until the editor is saved or closed. Assistive technology reads it as the description of that button, which takes the focus on the removal. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the removed dependent subject's group: its schema name, numbered where the field holds several of that schema ({{msg-mw|sws-dependent-subject-numbered}}).
sws-dependent-subject-undo:
Label of the button on the card of a dependent subject removed in the subject editor ({{msg-mw|sws-dependent-subject-removed}}), which brings the dependent subject back as it was.
{{Identical|Undo}}
sws-dependent-subject-numbered:
Name of one of several dependent subjects of one schema that a relation field of the subject editor shows inline, which tells them apart, for assistive technology and on their remove buttons. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the dependent subject's schema
* $2 - its position among the field's dependent subjects of that schema, starting at 1
sws-dependent-subject-load-error: Error shown inline in the subject editor in place of the fields of a dependent subject that could not be loaded.
sws-dependent-subject-add-error: Error notification when adding a dependent subject in the subject editor failed: no identifier could be fetched for it, the editor was saving, or the schema of the dependent subject had not loaded.
sws-subject-picker-placeholder: Placeholder text shown in the subject picker input field, which matches typed text against subject labels and accepts a complete subject ID.
sws-schema-picker-placeholder: Placeholder text shown in the schema picker input field and in the target schemas field of the schema property editor.
sws-schema-picker-create: Label of the option that starts creating a new schema, at the bottom of the dropdown of the schema picker and of the target schemas field of the schema property editor. Shown when the user has typed nothing.
sws-schema-picker-create-named:
Label of the option that starts creating a new schema named after what the user typed, at the bottom of the dropdown of the schema picker and of the target schemas field of the schema property editor. Parameters:
* $1 - the text the user typed, proposed as the new schema's name
sws-subject-picker-no-results: Message shown in the subject picker dropdown when no subjects match the search query.
sws-subject-picker-no-match: Error message shown in the subject picker when the user types text but does not select a subject from the dropdown results.
sws-subject-picker-create:
Label of an option at the bottom of the subject picker dropdown that creates a new subject, shown when the user has typed nothing. There is one such option for each schema the field accepts. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the schema the new subject will use
sws-subject-picker-create-named:
Label of an option at the bottom of the subject picker dropdown that creates a new subject named after what the user typed. There is one such option for each schema the field accepts. Parameters:
* $1 - the text the user typed, which becomes the new subject's label
* $2 - the name of the schema the new subject will use
sws-page-picker-placeholder: Placeholder text shown in the wiki page search input field.
sws-page-picker-no-results: Message shown in the page picker dropdown when no pages match the search query.
sws-page-picker-create-hint: Label of the unpickable option at the bottom of the page picker dropdown, shown while the user has typed nothing, telling them that typing a title offers a page that does not exist yet.
sws-page-picker-create-named:
Label of the option at the bottom of the page picker dropdown that picks a page which does not exist yet. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title the user typed
sws-schema-creator-title: Title of the dialog for creating a new schema.
sws-schema-creator-duplicate-title:
Title of the dialog for creating a new schema when it opens prefilled with a copy of an existing one, from {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-duplicate}} on [[Special:Schemas]]. 'Duplicate' is a verb.

Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the schema being duplicated
sws-schema-creator-button: Label of the button in the toolbar of [[Special:Schemas]] that opens the dialog for creating a schema.
sws-schema-creator-name-field: Label for the schema name input field in the schema creation dialog.
sws-schema-creator-name-placeholder: Placeholder text for the schema name input field in the schema creation dialog.
sws-schema-creator-name-required: Error shown when the schema name field is empty in the schema creation dialog.

sws-schema-creator-dependent: Label of the checkbox in the schema creator that declares the subjects of the new schema dependent.
