sws-schema-creator-dependent-info: Explanation of what the checkbox {{msg-mw|sws-schema-creator-dependent}} in the schema creator does, shown below it once the user presses the info button {{msg-mw|sws-schema-creator-dependent-info-label}}.
sws-schema-creator-dependent-info-label: Accessible name and tooltip of the info button next to the checkbox {{msg-mw|sws-schema-creator-dependent}} in the schema creator, which shows and hides {{msg-mw|sws-schema-creator-dependent-info}}.
sws-schema-creator-save: Label for the save button in the schema creation dialog.
sws-schema-creator-success: Success notification shown after creating a schema. $1 is the schema name.
sws-schema-creator-error: Error notification title shown when creating a schema fails. $1 is the schema name.
sws-schema-creator-summary-default: Default edit summary used when creating a schema via the UI.
sws-schemas-column-name: Column header for schema name in the schemas table on [[Special:Schemas]].
sws-schemas-column-description: Column header for schema description in the schemas table on [[Special:Schemas]].
sws-schemas-column-subjects:
Header of the column in the schema table on [[Special:Schemas]] that links to each schema's subjects, saying how many there are for readers who may see counts. It also holds the button that creates a subject of that schema.
{{Identical|Subjects}}
sws-schemas-empty: Message shown when no schemas exist yet on [[Special:Schemas]].
sws-schemas-export-button: Label of the button on [[Special:Schemas]] that downloads one JSON file with every schema the user can read.
sws-schemas-export-error: Title of the error notification shown when exporting the schemas fails.
sws-schemas-export-error-unreadable-sche:
Error notification shown, under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-export-error}}, when a schema could not be loaded during the schema export. Parameters:
* $1 - the schema name
sws-schemas-import-button: Label of the button on [[Special:Schemas]] that opens a file chooser for a schema export file, whose schemas can then be imported.
sws-schemas-import-error: Title of the error notification shown when the chosen file cannot be imported. The message under it says why.
sws-schemas-import-error-not-json: Error notification shown, under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-import-error}}, when the file chosen for the schema import is not JSON.
sws-schemas-import-error-no-schemas-obje: Error notification shown, under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-import-error}}, when the file chosen for the schema import lacks the top-level "schemas" object. "schemas" is a JSON key and must not be translated.
sws-schemas-import-error-empty: Error notification shown, under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-import-error}}, when the file chosen for the schema import holds no schemas.
sws-schemas-import-error-no-property-def:
Error notification shown, under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-import-error}}, when an entry of the file chosen for the schema import is not a schema. "propertyDefinitions" is a JSON key and must not be translated. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the entry
sws-schemas-import-error-unreadable-sche:
Error notification shown, under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-import-error}}, when a schema in the file chosen for the schema import cannot be read. Parameters:
* $1 - the schema name
* $2 - the reason, untranslated
sws-schemas-import-title: Title of the dialog that lists the schemas of the chosen file for import.
sws-schemas-import-new:
Heading, with a checkbox that checks them all, of the section of the import dialog that lists the schemas of the file that the wiki does not have. Parameters:
* $1 - the number of these schemas
sws-schemas-import-changed:
Heading, with a checkbox that checks them all, of the section of the import dialog that lists the schemas of the file that differ from the wiki's schemas of the same name. Parameters:
* $1 - the number of these schemas
sws-schemas-import-unchanged:
Heading of the section of the import dialog that names the schemas of the file that the wiki already has as they are, which are not imported. Parameters:
* $1 - the number of these schemas
sws-schemas-import-unchanged-names:
Shown under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-import-unchanged}} in the import dialog. Parameters:
* $1 - the names of the schemas, separated by {{msg-mw|comma-separator}}
sws-schemas-import-replaces:
Shown under {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-import-changed}} in the import dialog: importing a schema of that section replaces the wiki's schema of the same name. Parameters:
* $1 - the number of schemas in that section
sws-schemas-import-confirm:
Label of the button in the import dialog that imports the checked schemas. Parameters:
* $1 - the number of checked schemas
sws-schemas-import-failed:
Error message in the import dialog for a schema the import could not save. Parameters:
* $1 - the schema name
* $2 - the reason the save failed, as the wiki reported it
sws-schemas-import-summary: Edit summary used when a schema is saved by the schema import on [[Special:Schemas]].
sws-schemas-find: Placeholder and accessible name of the field on [[Special:Schemas]] that finds schemas by any part of their name.
sws-schemas-no-match:
Shown on [[Special:Schemas]] when no schema name contains the text in the find field.

Parameters:
* $1 - the text in the find field
sws-schemas-load-error: Shown on [[Special:Schemas]] in place of the schemas when they could not be loaded.
sws-schemas-view-list: Accessible name and tooltip of the toggle button on [[Special:Schemas]] that lists the schemas in a table.
sws-schemas-view-cards: Accessible name and tooltip of the toggle button on [[Special:Schemas]] that shows the schemas as cards.
sws-schemas-more-actions: Accessible name and tooltip of the menu button on each Schema card and table row on [[Special:Schemas]] that holds {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-duplicate}} and {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-delete}}.
sws-schemas-duplicate: Label of the item in the {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-more-actions}} menu of each Schema card and table row on [[Special:Schemas]] that opens the dialog for creating a schema, prefilled with a copy of that schema to be saved under a new name. 'Duplicate' is a verb.
sws-schemas-delete:
Label of the item in the {{msg-mw|sws-schemas-more-actions}} menu of each Schema card and table row on [[Special:Schemas]] that asks to confirm deleting that schema.
{{Identical|Delete}}
sws-schemas-create-subject:
Label of the button on each Schema card and table row on [[Special:Schemas]] that opens the 'create subject' dialog with that schema chosen. See also {{msg-mw|sws-schema-create-subject}}.
{{Identical|Create subject}}
sws-schema-sidebar-all-schemas: Label for the link in the SWS section of the sidebar on Schema pages that navigates to [[Special:Schemas]].
sws-sidebar-create-subject: Label for the link in the SWS section of the sidebar that navigates to [[Special:CreateSubject]], where a Subject is created together with a page of its own by default, or added to a page picked there. Shown only where {{msg-mw|sws-page-tools-create-subject}} is not, so a page carries one Create subject entry rather than two; the two read the same.
sws-schema-create-subject:
Label of the button that opens the 'create subject' dialog with a Schema chosen. Used on the Schema's own page, on [[Special:Subjects]] filtered to a Schema, and where {{#create_subject}} names a Schema.
Parameters:
* $1 - the Schema name
sws-schema-subject-count:
Link to [[Special:Subjects]] for one schema, saying how many subjects it has. Shown on each Schema card and table row on [[Special:Schemas]].

Parameters:
* $1 - the number of subjects, formatted for the user's language
sws-edit-schema: Label of the button that opens the schema editor on a schema's own page, and the accessible name and tooltip of the edit button on each Schema card and table row on [[Special:Schemas]].
sws-close-confirmation-title: Title of the confirmation dialog shown when closing a dialog with unsaved changes.
sws-close-confirmation-message: Message in the confirmation dialog asking the user to confirm discarding unsaved changes.
sws-close-confirmation-discard: Label for the destructive button that discards unsaved changes and closes the dialog.
sws-close-confirmation-keep-editing: Label for the button that dismisses the confirmation and returns to editing.
sws-schema-invalid:
Error message shown when saving an invalid Schema. Parameters:
* $1 - number of validation errors
* $2 - semicolon-separated list of the errors: {{msg-mw|sws-schema-invalid-detail}} for a structural error, or a message such as {{msg-mw|sws-property-name-reserved}} for a property name
sws-schema-invalid-detail:
One line of detail for a single Schema validation error. Parameters:
* $1 - JSON pointer to the location of the error
* $2 - the validation error message
sws-schema-name-invalid:
Error message shown when a Schema page title is not a valid schema name (empty or reserved). Parameters:
* $1 - the reason the name is invalid
sws-schema-dependence-unchangeable: Error shown when a save of a schema would change whether its subjects are dependent, which is set when the schema is created.
sws-schema-relation-targets-mixed:
Error shown when a save of a schema gives a relation property target schemas whose subjects are dependent together with target schemas whose subjects are standalone. Parameters:
* $1 - list of the names of the offending relation properties
* $2 - number of offending relation properties, for PLURAL
sws-property-name-not-canonical:
Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when a property name has spaces at its ends or several in a row. Parameters:
* $1 - the property name
* $2 - the property name as it must be written
sws-property-name-not-canonical-invisibl:
Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when a property name holds characters that cannot be seen or look like others, such as a zero-width space, a no-break space or a separately encoded accent. Parameters:
* $1 - the property name
* $2 - the property name as it must be written
* $3 - list of those characters as code points, such as "U+200B"
sws-property-name-empty: Shown among the errors of a refused schema save when a property name is empty or holds only spaces or invisible characters.
sws-property-name-characters:
Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when a property name holds a forbidden character: a control character, a noncharacter, U+FFFD, or one of # < > [ ] | { }. Parameters:
* $1 - the property name
* $2 - list of the characters; those that cannot be seen are given as code points, such as "U+0007"
sws-property-name-integer:
Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when a property name is an integer, such as 2024 or -1. Parameters:
* $1 - the property name
sws-property-name-dot-segment: Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when a property name is "." or "..".
sws-property-name-too-long:
Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when a property name takes more than 255 bytes in UTF-8. Parameters:
* $1 - the property name
sws-property-name-reserved:
Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when a property name is one SWS reserves: id, name, wiki_id or __proto__. Parameters:
* $1 - the property name
sws-property-name-near-duplicate:
Shown in the schema editor, and among the errors of a refused schema save, when two property names of one schema are the same apart from letter case, underscores in place of spaces, extra spaces, invisible characters, or compatibility variants such as full-width letters. Parameters:
* $1 - the property name
* $2 - the name of the other property
sws-layout-invalid:
Error message shown when saving an invalid Layout. Parameters:
* $1 - number of validation errors
* $2 - semicolon-separated list of {{msg-mw|sws-layout-invalid-detail}}, one per error
sws-layout-invalid-detail:
One line of detail for a single Layout validation error. Parameters:
* $1 - JSON pointer to the location of the error
* $2 - the validation error message
sws-layout-name-invalid:
Error message shown when a Layout page title is not a valid layout name (empty). Parameters:
* $1 - the reason the name is invalid
sws-mapping-invalid:
Error message shown when saving a structurally or semantically invalid ontology Mapping. Parameters:
* $1 - number of validation errors
* $2 - semicolon-separated list of {{msg-mw|sws-mapping-invalid-detail}}, one per error
sws-mapping-invalid-detail:
One line of detail for a single Mapping validation error. Parameters:
* $1 - JSON pointer to the location of the error
* $2 - the validation error message
sws-mapping-name-invalid:
Error message shown when a Mapping page title is not a valid mapping name (empty or the reserved name "native"). Parameters:
* $1 - the reason the name is invalid
sws-edit-layout: Aria label for the edit button on a Layout page.
sws-layout-display-schema: Label for the schema field in the layout display.
sws-layout-display-view-type: Label for the view type field in the layout display.
sws-layout-display-rules-caption: Caption for the display rules table in the layout display (hidden visually).
sws-layout-display-rule-property: Column header for the property name in the display rules table.
sws-layout-display-rule-type: Column header for the property type in the display rules table.
sws-layout-display-rule-attributes: Column header for display attributes in the display rules table.
sws-layout-display-no-rules: Message shown when a layout has no display rules, meaning all schema properties are shown in their default order.
sws-layout-sidebar-all-layouts: Label for the link in the SWS section of the sidebar on Layout pages that navigates to [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-editing-layout: Title of the dialog for editing a layout. $1 is the layout name.
sws-save-layout: Label for the save button in the layout editor dialog.
sws-edit-summary-help-text-layout: Help text shown below the edit summary in the layout editor dialog.
sws-delete-confirm-title: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before deleting a SWS page (Schema, Layout, or Mapping). $1 is the entity name.
sws-delete-confirm-message: Body of the delete confirmation dialog. $1 is the entity type noun (see sws-schema-noun etc.) followed by the entity name in bold, e.g. "schema '''Foo'''".
sws-delete-confirm-button: Label for the button that confirms deletion in the delete confirmation dialog.
sws-schema-noun: Lowercase common noun for a Schema, used inside sentences such as the delete confirmation message ("The schema Foo will be deleted").
sws-layout-noun: Lowercase common noun for a Layout, used inside sentences such as the delete confirmation message ("The layout Foo will be deleted").
sws-mapping-noun: Lowercase common noun for an ontology Mapping, used inside sentences such as the delete confirmation message ("The mapping Foo will be deleted").
sws-delete-reason-label: Label for the optional deletion-reason field in the delete confirmation dialog.
sws-delete-reason-placeholder: Placeholder for the optional deletion-reason field in the delete confirmation dialog.
sws-delete-summary-default: Default deletion reason recorded in the deletion log when the user enters none.
sws-delete-success: Success notification shown after a page is deleted. $1 is the page name.
sws-delete-error: Error notification title shown when deleting a page fails. $1 is the page name.
sws-layout-editor-description: Label for the description field in the layout editor.
sws-layout-editor-description-placeholde: Placeholder text for the description field in the layout editor.
sws-layout-editor-schema: Label for the read-only schema field in the layout editor.
sws-layout-editor-view-type: Label for the read-only view type field in the layout editor.
sws-layout-editor-show-all-properties: Label for the button that reveals all hidden properties, keeping the existing order of the shown ones.
sws-layout-editor-shown-count: Header in the display rule editor showing how many properties are visible. $1 is the number shown; $2 is the total number of properties.
sws-layout-editor-show-property: Aria label for the per-row toggle button that makes a hidden property visible in the display rule editor.
sws-layout-editor-hide-property: Aria label for the per-row toggle button that hides a visible property in the display rule editor.
sws-layout-editor-keep-one-shown: Tooltip on the disabled visibility toggle of the last shown property, explaining that at least one property must remain shown.
sws-layout-editor-summary-default: Default edit summary used when updating a layout via the UI.
sws-layout-editor-success: Success notification shown after updating a layout. $1 is the layout name.
sws-layout-editor-error: Error notification title shown when updating a layout fails. $1 is the layout name.
sws-layout-editor-schema-fetch-error: Error message shown in the layout editor when the schema properties could not be loaded.
sws-special-layouts: Title and description of the [[Special:Layouts]] page. Also the title of its card on [[Special:SWS]].
sws-layouts-column-name: Column header for layout name in the layouts list table on [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-layouts-column-schema: Column header for the schema name in the layouts list table on [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-layouts-column-type: Column header for the view type in the layouts list table on [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-layouts-column-description: Column header for layout description in the layouts list table on [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-layouts-empty: Message shown when no layouts exist yet on [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-special-mappings: Title and description of the [[Special:Mappings]] page, which lists the ontology mapping pages. Also the title of its card on [[Special:SWS]].
sws-mappings-column-name: Column header for mapping name in the mappings list table on [[Special:Mappings]].
sws-mappings-column-schemas: Column header for the mapped schemas in the mappings list table on [[Special:Mappings]]. The cell lists the mapped Schema names followed by their count.
sws-mappings-schema-count: Parenthesized count of mapped schemas, shown after the list of Schema names in a row of the mappings list table on [[Special:Mappings]]. $1 is the number of mapped schemas.
sws-mappings-schemas-none: Placeholder shown in the mapped-schemas cell of a row on [[Special:Mappings]] when the Mapping has no mapped Schemas.
sws-mappings-empty: Message shown when no mappings exist yet on [[Special:Mappings]].
sws-mapping-sidebar-all-mappings: Label for the link in the SWS section of the sidebar on Mapping pages that navigates to [[Special:Mappings]].
sws-mapping-creator-button: Label for the button that opens the mapping creation dialog on [[Special:Mappings]].
sws-mapping-creator-title: Title of the dialog for creating a new ontology mapping.
sws-mapping-creator-name-field: Label for the mapping name field in the mapping creation dialog.
sws-mapping-creator-name-placeholder: Placeholder text for the mapping name field in the mapping creation dialog.
sws-mapping-creator-name-required: Inline validation error shown when the mapping name field is left empty.
sws-mapping-creator-name-reserved: Inline validation error shown when the entered mapping name is the reserved projection name "native".
sws-mapping-creator-name-taken: Inline validation error shown when a mapping with the entered name already exists.
sws-mapping-creator-save: Label for the save button in the mapping creation dialog.
sws-mapping-creator-error: Error notification title shown when creating a mapping fails. $1 is the mapping name.
sws-mapping-creator-summary-default: Default edit summary used when creating a mapping via the UI.
sws-edit-mapping: Aria label for the edit button on a Mapping row in the mappings list.
sws-mapping-delete: Aria label for the delete button on a Mapping row in the mappings list.
sws-mapping-page-version:
Format version shown as a subtle line at the top of the read view of a Mapping page. Parameters:
* $1 - the mapping format version number
sws-mapping-page-schemas-heading: Heading for the overview table on the read view of a Mapping page that lists the mapped Schemas, each linked to its Schema page.
sws-mapping-page-schema-column: Column header for the Schema name in the mapped-schemas overview table on a Mapping page.
sws-mapping-page-class-column: Column header for the target ontology class in the mapped-schemas overview table on a Mapping page.
sws-mapping-page-properties-column: Column header for the number of mapped properties in the mapped-schemas overview table on a Mapping page.
sws-mapping-page-no-schemas: Message shown on the read view of a Mapping page that maps no Schemas. Tone matches {{msg-mw|sws-mappings-empty}}.
sws-mapping-page-prefixes-heading: Heading for the table on the read view of a Mapping page that lists the namespace prefixes the mapping declares.
sws-mapping-page-prefix-column: Column header for the prefix in the prefixes table on a Mapping page.
sws-mapping-page-namespace-column: Column header for the namespace IRI in the prefixes table on a Mapping page.
sws-mapping-unsupported-version:
Warning shown above the JSON of a Mapping page written in a format version this SWS cannot read. Parameters:
* $1 - the format version found on the page
sws-mapping-docs-pointer:
Notice shown above the editor on a page in the Mapping namespace. Parameters:
* $1 - the URL of the Mapping format documentation
sws-layout-creator-title: Title of the dialog for creating a new layout.
sws-layout-creator-button: Label for the button that opens the layout creation dialog on [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-layout-creator-name-field: Label for the layout name input field in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-name-placeholder: Placeholder text for the layout name input field in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-name-required: Error shown when the layout name field is empty in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-name-taken: Error shown when a layout with the entered name already exists in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-schema-field: Label for the schema selector in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-view-type-field: Label for the view type selector in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-view-type-placeholder: Placeholder text for the view type selector in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-save: Label for the save button in the layout creation dialog.
sws-layout-creator-success: Success notification shown after creating a layout. $1 is the layout name.
sws-layout-creator-error: Error notification title shown when creating a layout fails. $1 is the layout name.
sws-layout-creator-summary-default: Default edit summary used when creating a layout via the UI.
sws-layout-delete: Aria label for the delete button on a Layout row in the layouts list.
sws-property-type-select: Label for the select/dropdown property type shown in the property type selector.
sws-property-editor-name-required: Error shown under the property name field in the schema editor when the name is empty.
sws-property-editor-name-taken: Error shown under the property name field in the schema editor when another property of the schema already has the entered name. $1 is the entered name.
sws-property-editor-min-exceeds-max: Error shown in the schema editor when the minimum value exceeds the maximum value for a number property.
sws-property-editor-options: Label for the options field in the select property type editor, where schema creators define the allowed values.
sws-property-editor-options-unique: Error shown under each option whose label is the same as another option's (ignoring letter case and surrounding spaces), in the options list of a Select property in the schema editor, and in the notification that refuses the save.
sws-property-editor-option:
Accessible name, read out by screen readers, of the field holding an option's label in the options list of a Select property in the schema editor.

Parameters:
* $1 - the option's position in the list, starting at 1
sws-property-editor-option-label-require: Error shown under an option without a label in the options list of a Select property in the schema editor, and in the notification that refuses the save.
sws-property-editor-move-option-up:
Accessible name and tooltip of the button that moves an option one place up the options list of a Select property in the schema editor.

Parameters:
* $1 - the option's position in the list, starting at 1
sws-property-editor-move-option-down:
Accessible name and tooltip of the button that moves an option one place down the options list of a Select property in the schema editor.

Parameters:
* $1 - the option's position in the list, starting at 1
sws-property-editor-remove-option:
Accessible name and tooltip of the button that removes an option from the options list of a Select property in the schema editor.

Parameters:
* $1 - the option's position in the list, starting at 1
sws-property-editor-add-option: Button under the options list of a Select property in the schema editor. Adds an option without a label to the end of the list.
sws-property-editor-option-moved:
Announced to screen reader users when an option moves up or down the options list of a Select property in the schema editor.

Parameters:
* $1 - the option's new position in the list, starting at 1
* $2 - the number of options in the list
sws-property-editor-option-removed: Announced to screen reader users when an option is removed from the options list of a Select property in the schema editor.
sws-property-editor-single-value: Name of the single-value Constraint in the schema editor, used as $1 in {{msg-mw|sws-severity-input-label}} for the severity control next to {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-multiple}}. The Constraint applies while multiple values are not allowed, so it cannot be named after that checkbox. {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values-one}} names the same Constraint for Text with language, so the two should match.
sws-property-editor-values: Label of the group of options in the schema editor that sets how many values a property of type {{msg-mw|sws-property-type-monolingualtext}} takes: {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values-one}}, {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values-one-per-language}} or {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values-multiple-per-language}}.
sws-property-editor-values-one: Option of {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values}}: the property takes one text, in one language. Also names this Constraint as $1 in {{msg-mw|sws-severity-input-label}}.
sws-property-editor-values-one-help: One-line example under the option {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values-one}}: something that has a single text in a single language.
sws-property-editor-values-one-per-langu: Option of {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values}}: the property takes at most one text in each language, such as the translations of one caption. Also names this Constraint as $1 in {{msg-mw|sws-severity-input-label}}.
One-line example under the option {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values-one-per-language}}: something that has one text in each language.
sws-property-editor-values-multiple-per-: Option of {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values}}: the property takes any number of texts, including several in one language.
One-line example under the option {{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-values-multiple-per-language}}: something that can have several texts in one language.
sws-severity-warning:
Name of the warning severity level of a Constraint: a violation is flagged but never blocks saving. Shown in the severity control's menu in the schema editor and as $1 in {{msg-mw|sws-severity-input-label}}.
{{Identical|Warning}}
sws-severity-warning-description: One-line meaning of the warning severity level, shown under {{msg-mw|sws-severity-warning}} in the severity control's menu in the schema editor. A constraint violation is the finding a Constraint yields when data does not satisfy it; marking them as warnings reports them to editors without ever rejecting a save. Parallel to {{msg-mw|sws-severity-error-description-not-enforced}}, which differs only in the severity named.
sws-severity-error:
Name of the error severity level of a Constraint: a violation can block saving when the wiki enforces validation. Shown in the severity control's menu in the schema editor and as $1 in {{msg-mw|sws-severity-input-label}}.
{{Identical|Error}}
sws-severity-error-description-enforced: One-line meaning of the error severity level on a wiki that enforces validation, shown under {{msg-mw|sws-severity-error}} in the severity control's menu in the schema editor. "New" is load-bearing: such a wiki rejects only writes that introduce a violation that was not already present, so Subjects that are already invalid stay editable. See also {{msg-mw|sws-severity-error-description-not-enforced}}.
sws-severity-error-description-not-enfor: One-line meaning of the error severity level on a wiki that does not enforce validation, shown under {{msg-mw|sws-severity-error}} in the severity control's menu in the schema editor. Nothing blocks saving on such a wiki, so the level only decides how violations are reported to editors. Parallel to {{msg-mw|sws-severity-warning-description}}, which differs only in the severity named. See also {{msg-mw|sws-severity-error-description-enforced}}.
sws-property-editor-target-schema: Label for the target schemas field in the schema property editor. Selects the schemas of the subjects a relation may point to.
sws-property-editor-target-schema-requir: Validation error shown when a relation property has no target schema.
sws-property-editor-target-schema-depend: Shown in place of results in the menu of the target schemas field of the schema editor ({{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-target-schema}}), when the property's target schemas have dependent subjects and the typed text finds only schemas whose subjects are standalone, which a property cannot mix with them.
sws-property-editor-target-schema-standa: Shown in place of results in the menu of the target schemas field of the schema editor ({{msg-mw|sws-property-editor-target-schema}}), when the property's target schemas have standalone subjects and the typed text finds only schemas whose subjects are dependent, which a property cannot mix with them.
sws-field-invalid-option: Validation error shown when a selected value is not in the allowed options list. $1 is the invalid value.
sws-field-single-value-only: Validation message shown when a property that allows only one value holds several.
sws-field-single-value-per-language: Validation message shown under a value of a property of type {{msg-mw|sws-property-type-monolingualtext}} when an earlier value is in the same language and the property allows one value per language.
sws-field-type-mismatch: Validation error shown when a Statement's stored type no longer matches the property's current type (e.g. the Schema changed after the value was saved). $1 is the type the value was written as; $2 is the type the property now expects.
sws-field-schema-not-found: Form-level error shown when the backend reports the Subject's Schema page is missing. $1 is the schema name.
sws-field-unregistered-type: Validation warning shown when a Statement's Property Type is not registered, because the extension providing it is disabled or failed to load. The value is preserved but cannot be displayed or edited. $1 is the property type name.
sws-field-min-length: Validation error shown when a text value is shorter than the property's minimum length. $1 is the minimum number of characters.
sws-field-max-length: Validation error shown when a text value is longer than the property's maximum length. $1 is the maximum number of characters.
sws-field-relation-target-schema-mismatc: Validation error shown when a relation points to a subject whose schema is none of the relation's target schemas. $1 is the schema the target subject uses.
sws-field-relation-target-not-found: Validation warning shown when a relation points to a subject ID the wiki cannot resolve for this user, either because no such subject exists or because it lives on a page the user may not read. $1 is the target subject ID. Word it so it does not assert the subject is absent, which would be wrong in the second case. Non-blocking: the target may be created later (for example during import), mirroring wiki red links.
sws-field-relation-target-unresolvable-s: Validation error shown when a relation points to a subject ID whose source key names a subject source this wiki has not registered. $1 is the target subject ID, in its "sourceKey:localId" form. Severity error: like every other error, it blocks the write only when the wiki enforces validation.
sws-field-dependent-subject-referenced-t: Error shown when a save would make more than one relation point to the same dependent subject: a subject of a schema that declares its subjects dependent, which only the relation from its host subject may point to. It blocks the save whatever the wiki's validation enforcement setting.
sws-field-dependent-target-not-on-page:
Error shown on a relation property whose target schemas have dependent subjects, when it points to a subject that is not on the same page. It blocks the save whatever the wiki's validation enforcement setting. Parameters:
* $1 - the ID of the subject the relation points to
sws-field-relation-to-dependent-subject:
Error shown when a relation points to a dependent subject from a property whose target schemas do not have dependent subjects, or from a property the schema does not declare. It blocks the save whatever the wiki's validation enforcement setting. Parameters:
* $1 - the ID of the dependent subject the relation points to
sws-field-dependent-subject-is-main: Error shown when a save would make a dependent subject the main subject of its page. It blocks the save whatever the wiki's validation enforcement setting.
sws-field-dependent-subject-has-label: Error shown when a save would give a dependent subject a label: dependent subjects are named after their schema and their host subject. It blocks the save whatever the wiki's validation enforcement setting.
sws-field-dependent-subject-without-host: Error shown when a save would put a dependent subject on a page where no subject points to it: when one is created on its own, or moved without its host subject. It blocks the save whatever the wiki's validation enforcement setting.
sws-select-placeholder: Placeholder text shown in the select dropdown before any option is chosen.
sws-select-no-results: Message shown in the multi-select dropdown when the typed text does not match any available option.
sws-field-invalid-number: Validation error shown under a number field whose text cannot be interpreted as a number. Also shown as an error notification, titled with the property name, when an action is held because a number field holds such text.
sws-field-invalid-datetime: Validation error shown under a date and time field whose entry is incomplete, such as one with a part cleared, or cannot be parsed. Also shown as an error notification, titled with the property name, when an action is held because the field holds such an entry. DateTime values must be strict ISO 8601 / xsd:dateTime strings with an explicit timezone offset or 'Z' (for example, '2025-06-15T12:00:00Z' or '2025-06-15T12:00:00+02:00'). Partial values such as year-only or date-only are rejected, and min/max bounds are inclusive.
sws-property-type-datetime: Label for the date and time property type in the schema editor
sws-field-invalid-date: Validation error shown under a date field whose entry is incomplete, such as one with a part cleared, or cannot be parsed. Also shown as an error notification, titled with the property name, when an action is held because the field holds such an entry. Date values must be strict ISO 8601 calendar dates in YYYY-MM-DD form with no time or timezone component (for example, '2025-06-15'). Values with a time part, partial values such as year-only, and calendar overflows such as '2025-02-30' are rejected, and min/max bounds are inclusive.
sws-property-type-date: Label for the date (without time) property type in the schema editor
sws-property-type-boolean: Label for the boolean (true/false) property type shown in the property type selector.
sws-property-type-monolingualtext: Label of the property type whose values are texts, each with the language it is in (monolingualText), shown in the property type selector.
sws-monolingual-text-more-languages:
Link under a monolingual text value in a View that reveals the texts in the languages not shown to the reader.

Parameters:
* $1 - how many languages those texts are in
sws-monolingual-text-fewer-languages: Link under a monolingual text value in a View, after the texts revealed by {{msg-mw|sws-monolingual-text-more-languages}}, that hides them again.
sws-monolingual-text-text-label: Accessible label of a monolingual text value's text field in the subject editor. $1 is the property name, $2 the value's position in the list, starting at 1.
sws-monolingual-text-language-label: Accessible name of the language list beside a monolingual text value's text field in the subject editor. $1 is the property name, $2 the value's position, starting at 1.
sws-language-input-other: Last entry of the language list beside a monolingual text field in the subject editor. Opens a search over every language.
sws-language-picker-placeholder: Placeholder and accessible name of the search field in the language panel of a monolingual text field in the subject editor.
sws-language-picker-no-results: Message shown in the language panel of a monolingual text field when the search matches no language.
sws-language-picker-tag: Description of the language menu entry offering a tag the user typed, when MediaWiki has no language name for it. Marks that entry as a tag rather than a language name.
sws-property-type-unregistered: Label shown in place of a property type name when the type is not registered (e.g. owned by a disabled or failed extension).
sws-property-type-unregistered-note: Muted note shown next to a value whose property type is not registered. $1 is the stored type name (e.g. 'color').
sws-property-type-unregistered-input-not: Muted note shown in the value editor for a property whose type is not registered, explaining the value is read-only and preserved unchanged. $1 is the stored type name.
sws-property-type-unregistered-attribute: Muted note shown in the schema property editor in place of the type-specific attribute inputs when the property type is not registered, explaining the stored settings are preserved but not editable.
sws-property-type-unregistered-notificat: Warning notification shown once per page when it contains data of a property type that is not registered (e.g. owned by a disabled or failed extension). $1 is the stored type name.
sws-boolean-true: Label shown in the value display for a boolean property whose value is true (e.g. in the infobox or schema-table 'Initial value' column).
sws-boolean-false: Label shown in the value display for a boolean property whose value is false (e.g. in the infobox or schema-table 'Initial value' column).
sws-select-unknown-option: Placeholder shown in a select-property display when a stored option ID cannot be resolved to a label (e.g. the option was removed from the Schema).
sws-managesubjects-tab: Label for the Data tab that appears alongside the standard action tabs (View, Edit, History) on content pages, linking to the Subject management page.
sws-managesubjects-title: Title of the Subject management page. $1 is the prefixed page title (e.g. 'Berlin').
sws-managesubjects-not-applicable: Error shown when the Subject management page is opened on a page that cannot have Subjects (e.g. a Special page or a non-existent page).
sws-managesubjects-add-button: Label for the button that opens the Subject creation flow from the Subject management page.
sws-managesubjects-empty-title: Heading of the large zero-state shown on the Subject management page when the page has neither a Main Subject nor any other Subjects.
sws-managesubjects-empty-description: Descriptive subtitle below {{msg-mw|sws-managesubjects-empty-title}} explaining what Subjects are and inviting the user to add one.
sws-managesubjects-no-main-title: Heading of the placeholder shown in the Main Subject slot when the page has other Subjects but no Main Subject assigned.
sws-managesubjects-no-main-description: Subtitle under {{msg-mw|sws-managesubjects-no-main-title}} explaining how to assign a Main Subject and what the Main Subject represents.
sws-managesubjects-count: Subtle text on the Subject management toolbar showing the total number of Subjects on the page. $1 is the count.
sws-managesubjects-main-subject-set: Notification confirming a Subject was promoted to Main Subject. $1 is the name the subject is shown under, read after the promotion, so it names the page rather than being a stand-in. Keep the quotation marks around it.
sws-managesubjects-main-subject-cleared: Notification confirming the page no longer has a Main Subject.
sws-managesubjects-reordered: Notification confirming the subjects on the page were reordered via drag.
sws-managesubjects-ordering-error: Notification shown when a drag operation (reorder, promote, demote) failed to persist.
sws-managesubjects-main-subject-error: Notification shown when changing the Main Subject failed.
sws-managesubjects-main-subject-indicato: Accessible label and tooltip for the pin icon that marks a row as the Main Subject of the page.
sws-managesubjects-other-subjects-headin: Heading above the list of non-main Subjects on the Subject management page.
sws-managesubjects-row-edit: Aria/button label for editing a Subject from its row.
sws-managesubjects-row-delete: Aria/button label for deleting a Subject from its row.
sws-managesubjects-row-move: Label and tooltip of the button that opens the dialog for moving a subject to another page.
sws-managesubjects-move-title: Title of the dialog for moving a subject to another page.
sws-managesubjects-move-target-label: Label of the field naming the page the subject is moved to.
sws-managesubjects-move-creates-page:
Note shown when the chosen target page does not exist yet. Parameters:
* $1 - the title of the page that will be created
sws-managesubjects-move-make-main: Label of the checkbox that makes the moved subject the main subject of the page it is moved to. Says "the target page" rather than "this page", which in this UI means the page being viewed.
sws-managesubjects-move-demotes:
Note shown under the main-subject checkbox when the target page already has a main subject, which the move would demote to one of the page's other subjects. Parameters:
* $1 - the display name of the target page's current main subject
sws-managesubjects-move-source-loses-mai:
Warning shown when the subject being moved is the main subject of the page it is moved away from. Parameters:
* $1 - the title of the page the subject is moved away from
sws-managesubjects-move-confirm-button: Label of the button that performs the move.
sws-managesubjects-move-success:
Notification shown after a subject was moved. Parameters:
* $1 - the display name of the moved subject
* $2 - a link to the page it was moved to, labelled with that page's title
sws-managesubjects-move-error:
Notification shown when moving a subject failed for an unrecognised reason. Parameters:
* $1 - the display name of the subject that could not be moved
sws-managesubjects-move-page-taken: Error shown when the page the move was going to create already exists.
sws-managesubjects-move-create-page-summ: Default edit summary for the empty page created to hold a moved subject.
sws-managesubjects-move-create-page-erro:
Error shown when the target page could not be created. Parameters:
* $1 - the title of the page that could not be created
sws-managesubjects-row-promote: Aria/button label for the pin button that promotes one of the page's other Subjects to its Main Subject.
sws-managesubjects-row-demote: Aria/button label for the pin button on the Main Subject row that clears it so the page has no Main Subject.
sws-managesubjects-row-copy-link: Aria/button label for the row action (an inline button on wide viewports, an overflow-menu item on narrow ones) that copies a shareable link to this Subject.
sws-managesubjects-row-more: Aria/button label for the overflow (kebab) menu that lists per-row actions on narrow viewports.
sws-managesubjects-row-drag-handle: Tooltip on the drag handle on each Subject row (sighted mouse users only — the handle is not in the focus order). Dragging a row within the list of other Subjects reorders it. Dragging such a row onto the Main Subject slot promotes it (and demotes the previous main into the dragged row's slot). Dragging the Main Subject row into the list of other Subjects demotes it at the drop position.
sws-managesubjects-statement-count: Shown on each collapsed Subject row to indicate how many Statements the Subject has. $1 is the count.
sws-managesubjects-no-statements: Empty-state shown inside an expanded Subject row when the Subject has no statements.
sws-managesubjects-delete-summary-defaul: Default edit summary used when deleting a Subject from the Subject management page.
sws-managesubjects-delete-confirm-title: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before deleting a Subject.
sws-managesubjects-delete-confirm-messag: Body of the delete confirmation dialog. $1 is the name the subject is shown under, rendered in bold, which is why it carries no quotation marks.
sws-managesubjects-delete-confirm-remove:
Second paragraph of the delete confirmation dialog ({{msg-mw|sws-managesubjects-delete-confirm-message}}) for a dependent subject: deleting it also removes the relation to it from its host subject. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the host subject

As {{msg-mw|sws-managesubjects-delete-confirm-removed-from-host}}, for a dependent subject that holds dependent subjects of its own, which are deleted with it. Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the host subject
sws-managesubjects-delete-confirm-button: Label for the destructive confirm-button in the delete dialog.
sws-managesubjects-delete-success: Notification confirming a Subject was deleted.
sws-managesubjects-delete-error: Notification shown when deleting a Subject failed. $1 is the name the subject is shown under: a stored label, or the subject's bracketed identifier, such as "(s1ab2cd3ef4gh5i)", for a subject nobody named. Keep the quotation marks around it, because a stored label is arbitrary text and needs delimiting.
sws-managesubjects-load-error: Notification shown when loading the Subject list for the page failed.
sws-managesubjects-id-label: Inline label shown before the Subject ID in the footer of an expanded Subject row. Typically short, e.g. "ID:".
sws-managesubjects-id-copy: Tooltip and accessible name of the subject ID button, which copies the ID to the clipboard when clicked. $1 is the Subject ID.
sws-managesubjects-id-copied: Notification shown after the subject ID was copied. $1 is the Subject ID.
sws-managesubjects-id-copy-error: Notification shown when copying the subject ID to the clipboard failed.
sws-managesubjects-iri-label: Inline label shown before the Subject IRI (its RDF concept URI) in the footer of an expanded Subject row. Typically short, e.g. "IRI:".
sws-managesubjects-iri-copy: Tooltip on the subject IRI button. $1 is the Subject IRI. Click copies the IRI to the clipboard.
sws-managesubjects-iri-copied: Notification shown after the subject IRI was copied. $1 is the Subject IRI.
sws-managesubjects-iri-copy-error: Notification shown when copying the subject IRI to the clipboard failed.
sws-managesubjects-link-copied: Notification shown after the deep link to a Subject's row was copied to the clipboard. Takes no parameters.
sws-managesubjects-link-copy-error: Notification shown when copying the deep link to the clipboard failed.
sws-managesubjects-export-json: Label of the button that opens the raw JSON representation of a Subject in a new tab. See {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-all-json}} for all Subjects on the page. "JSON" is the format name and is not translated.
sws-managesubjects-export-rdf: Label of the button that opens the menu of RDF exports of a Subject. See {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-all-rdf}} for all Subjects on the page. "RDF" is the name of the data model and is not translated.
sws-managesubjects-export-all-json: Label of the button in the Data-tab header that opens the raw JSON representation of all Subjects on the page in a new tab. "JSON" is the format name and is not translated.
sws-managesubjects-export-all-rdf: Label of the button in the Data-tab header that opens the menu of RDF exports of all Subjects on the page. "RDF" is the name of the data model and is not translated.
sws-managesubjects-export-format-turtle: RDF export menu item that opens the Turtle serialization in a new tab, when the menu offers a single projection; otherwise $2 of {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-projection-format}}. "Turtle" is the RDF serialization format name and is not translated.
sws-managesubjects-export-format-trig: RDF export menu item that opens the TriG serialization in a new tab, when the menu offers a single projection; otherwise $2 of {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-projection-format}}. "TriG" is the RDF serialization format name and is not translated.
sws-managesubjects-export-projection-for:
RDF export menu item, when the menu offers several projections. A projection is a named RDF rendering of the data, e.g. EDM or CIDOC-CRM.

Parameters:
* $1 - the projection: {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-native}}, or the name of an ontology Mapping
* $2 - the serialization format: {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-format-turtle}} or {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-format-trig}}
sws-managesubjects-export-native: Display name of the native (SWS-vocabulary) RDF projection, $1 of {{msg-sws|sws-managesubjects-export-projection-format}}.
action-subjects: Description of the Subject management action used by MediaWiki when generating action descriptions.
sws-config-invalid: Heading shown above the list of errors when an edit to the MediaWiki:SWS JSON configuration page is rejected.
sws-config-error-not-object: Error shown when the content of the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page is not a JSON object.
sws-config-error-unknown-key: Error shown when the configuration contains a setting that is not exposed on-wiki. $1 is the unknown key.
sws-config-error-invalid-boolean: Error shown when a setting that must be a boolean is not. $1 is the setting key. The words "true" and "false" are literal JSON values and must not be translated.
sws-config-error-invalid-language-list: Error shown when a setting that must be a list of language tags is not. $1 is the setting key. The example ["de", "fr", "it"] is a literal JSON value and must not be translated.
sws-config-type-boolean: Accepted-value description in the configuration reference table for a boolean setting. Contains HTML: the literal JSON values "true" and "false", each wrapped in a <code> tag, must not be translated.
sws-config-type-language-list: Accepted-value description in the configuration reference table for a setting that lists language tags. Contains HTML: the example JSON value, wrapped in a <code> tag, must not be translated.
sws-config-docs-heading: Heading of the configuration reference shown on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page. Also the link target of {{msg-sws|sws-config-docs-pointer}}.
sws-config-docs-pointer:
One-line pointer shown above the JSON editor of the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.

Parameters:
* $1 - the anchor of the on-page reference
* $2 - the URL of the external documentation
sws-config-docs-column-key: Column header in the configuration reference table for the setting key written on the page.
sws-config-docs-column-value: Column header in the configuration reference table for the value the setting accepts.
sws-config-docs-column-setting: Column header in the configuration reference table for the LocalSettings.php setting that the page key overrides.
sws-config-setting-subject-first: Label of the choice between {{msg-sws|sws-config-setting-subject-first-page-first}} and {{msg-sws|sws-config-setting-subject-first-subject-first}}, the subjectFirst setting, in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page. See https://neowiki.ai/docs/glossary#page-first-and-subject-first-wikis
sws-config-setting-subject-first-page-fi: Option of {{msg-sws|sws-config-setting-subject-first}} in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page: the wiki is page-first. See https://neowiki.ai/docs/glossary#page-first-and-subject-first-wikis
One-line description under the option {{msg-sws|sws-config-setting-subject-first-page-first}}, saying what a page-first wiki does.
sws-config-setting-subject-first-subject: Option of {{msg-sws|sws-config-setting-subject-first}} in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page: the wiki is subject-first. See https://neowiki.ai/docs/glossary#page-first-and-subject-first-wikis
One-line description under the option {{msg-sws|sws-config-setting-subject-first-subject-first}}, saying what a subject-first wiki does.
sws-config-setting-enforce-validation: Label of the checkbox for the enforceValidation setting in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page. Checked, an edit that newly violates a constraint whose severity is {{msg-sws|sws-severity-error}} is not saved.
sws-config-setting-auto-render-main-subj: Label of the checkbox for the autoRenderMainSubject setting in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page. Checked, every page shows its Main Subject without the page asking for one: as an infobox, or in full on a subject-first wiki.
sws-config-setting-data-languages-help: One-line help under {{msg-sws|sws-config-setting-data-languages}} in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page. The editor of a text with its language offers these languages in the order of the list, with every other language a search away.
sws-config-editor-title: Heading and browser tab title of the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page where it shows the settings form, in place of the page name.
sws-config-editor-edit-source-tab: Label of the tab that opens the JSON editor of the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page, shown to someone who may change the settings, beside the tab of the settings form, which reads {{msg-mw|skin-view-edit}}.
sws-config-editor-intro: Line at the top of the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page, shown to a user who may change the settings. "LocalSettings.php" is the name of the server's configuration file and must not be translated.
sws-config-editor-read-only: Shown at the top of the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page to a user who may not edit the page, in place of {{msg-sws|sws-config-editor-intro}}.
sws-config-editor-reset: Link under a setting in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page, shown when the page sets that setting. Stops the page from setting it, so the default from the server's configuration applies again.
sws-config-editor-save: Button that saves the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.
sws-config-editor-saved: Notification shown once the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page is saved.
sws-config-editor-save-failed:
Error shown under the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page when saving it fails.

Parameters:
* $1 - the reason the save failed, as the wiki or the browser reports it, such as the explanation of a missing permission or of an edit conflict
sws-config-editor-changed-meanwhile: Warning shown under the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page after a save the wiki merged with another change to the page, made after the form was loaded, by someone else or in another tab. The form cannot save again until the page is reloaded.
sws-config-editor-add-language: Button under the list of languages in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page. Opens a search over every language, to add one to the end of the list.
sws-config-editor-move-language-up:
Accessible name and tooltip of the button that moves a language one place up the list in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.

Parameters:
* $1 - the language's name, or its language tag when MediaWiki has no name for it
sws-config-editor-move-language-down:
Accessible name and tooltip of the button that moves a language one place down the list in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.

Parameters:
* $1 - the language's name, or its language tag when MediaWiki has no name for it
sws-config-editor-remove-language:
Accessible name and tooltip of the button that removes a language from the list in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.

Parameters:
* $1 - the language's name, or its language tag when MediaWiki has no name for it
sws-config-editor-language-added:
Announced to screen reader users when a language is added to the list in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.

Parameters:
* $1 - the language's name, or its language tag when MediaWiki has no name for it
sws-config-editor-language-moved:
Announced to screen reader users when a language moves up or down the list in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.

Parameters:
* $1 - the language's name, or its language tag when MediaWiki has no name for it
* $2 - its new position in the list, starting at 1
* $3 - how many languages the list holds
sws-config-editor-language-removed:
Announced to screen reader users when a language is removed from the list in the form on the MediaWiki:SWS configuration page.

Parameters:
* $1 - the language's name, or its language tag when MediaWiki has no name for it
sws-special-graphstores: Title and description of the [[Special:GraphStores]] page, which reports and rebuilds the wiki's graph stores. Also the title of its card on [[Special:SWS]].
sws-graphstores-intro: Introduction shown above the store table on [[Special:GraphStores]].
sws-graphstores-nostores: Shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] instead of the introduction and the store table when no graph store is configured.
sws-graphstores-column-store:
Column heading on [[Special:GraphStores]]: the store's configured name.
{{Identical|Store}}
sws-graphstores-column-projection: Column heading on [[Special:GraphStores]]: the RDF vocabulary the store holds.
sws-graphstores-column-state:
Column heading on [[Special:GraphStores]]: how far the store is from the wiki.
{{Identical|State}}
sws-graphstores-column-lastrebuild: Column heading on [[Special:GraphStores]]: when the store was last rebuilt successfully.
sws-graphstores-column-actions:
Column heading on [[Special:GraphStores]]: the buttons that start or stop a rebuild.
{{Identical|Actions}}
sws-graphstores-projection-none:
{{optional}}
Shown in the projection column on [[Special:GraphStores]] for a backend that holds no RDF, such as Neo4j. The English message is an em dash.
sws-graphstores-state-insync: State on [[Special:GraphStores]]: the store's copy matches the wiki.
sws-graphstores-state-stale:
State on [[Special:GraphStores]]: the Mapping page defining the store's projection was edited or deleted after that store's last successful rebuild started, so the store still describes pages with the old vocabulary.

Parameters:
* $1 - when that Mapping page last changed, already formatted as a date and time in the user's language
sws-graphstores-state-neverbuilt: State on [[Special:GraphStores]]: no rebuild of this store ever reconciled the whole wiki — it never ran, or every run so far left pages failed.
sws-graphstores-state-queued: State on [[Special:GraphStores]]: a rebuild has been queued but has not started.
sws-graphstores-state-running:
State on [[Special:GraphStores]]: a rebuild is under way.

Parameters:
* $1 - number of pages projected so far
* $2 - number of pages the rebuild could not reconcile
sws-graphstores-lastrebuild:
Last rebuild column on [[Special:GraphStores]], for the store's last successful rebuild.

Parameters:
* $1 - when that rebuild finished, already formatted as a date and time in the user's language
* $2 - number of pages it projected
* $3 - number of pages it could not reconcile
sws-graphstores-lastrebuild-never:
Shown in the last rebuild column on [[Special:GraphStores]] when no rebuild of the store has ever succeeded.
{{Identical|Never}}
sws-graphstores-rebuild: Label of the button on [[Special:GraphStores]] that queues a rebuild of one store.
sws-graphstores-cancel: Label of the button on [[Special:GraphStores]] that stops the rebuild a store has queued or running.
sws-graphstores-outcome-queued:
Confirmation shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] after queueing a rebuild.

Parameters:
* $1 - name of the graph store
sws-graphstores-outcome-cancelled:
Confirmation shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] after cancelling a rebuild.

Parameters:
* $1 - name of the graph store
sws-graphstores-outcome-alreadyrunning:
Error shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] when a rebuild was asked for a store that already has one.

Parameters:
* $1 - name of the graph store
sws-graphstores-outcome-nothingtocancel:
Error shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] when a cancellation was asked for a store with no rebuild.

Parameters:
* $1 - name of the graph store
sws-graphstores-outcome-unknownstore:
Error shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] when the named store is not configured.

Parameters:
* $1 - name that was asked for
sws-graphstores-outcome-notqueued:
Error shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] when a rebuild could not be started at all — the job queue refused it, or something else held the store's start lock.

Parameters:
* $1 - name of the graph store
sws-graphstores-outcome-sessionfailure: Error shown on [[Special:GraphStores]] when the edit token of a rebuild or cancel form did not match.
sws-special-subject:
Name of the [[Special:Subject]] page, which shows one Subject. Used as the page's heading when it shows no Subject.
{{Identical|Subject}}
sws-special-subject-invalid-id: Error shown on [[Special:Subject]] when its subpage is not a subject ID. The example ID stays as it is.
sws-special-subject-page-label: Inline label shown before a link to the wiki page a Subject is stored on, in the footer of an expanded Subject row.
sws-special-subject-referenced-heading: Heading on [[Special:Subject]] above the Subjects the displayed Subject's relations point at.
sws-special-subject-not-found:
Shown on [[Special:Subject]] in place of the Subject when the wiki has no Subject with that ID. It is also shown for a Subject on a page the reader may not read, so the translation must not mention permissions.

Parameters:
* $1 - the Subject ID that was asked for
sws-special-subject-load-error: Shown on [[Special:Subject]] when loading a Subject failed with a network or server error: in place of the Subject on first load, and as a notification when a re-read after a change failed. Distinct from {{msg-sws|sws-special-subject-not-found}}, which says the wiki has no such Subject.
sws-managesubjects-row-open: Label for the item in a Subject row's overflow menu that goes to [[Special:Subject]], the page showing that one Subject. It navigates; it does not expand the row. The overflow menu replaces the row's inline actions on narrow viewports.
sws-special-subject-referenced-by-headin: Heading on [[Special:Subject]] above the Subjects whose relations point at the displayed Subject. The opposite direction of {{msg-sws|sws-special-subject-referenced-heading}}.
sws-special-subject-referenced-by-trunca:
Shown on [[Special:Subject]] below the list of Subjects referencing the displayed one, when more exist than the list shows. The total is unknown, so the translation must not imply one.

Parameters:
* $1 - the number of Subjects listed
sws-create-subject-default-label:
Label of the button {{#create_subject}} places on a page to open the 'create subject' dialog. Used when the wikitext gives neither a label nor a Schema; with a Schema, {{msg-sws|sws-schema-create-subject}} is used instead.
{{Identical|Create subject}}
sws-create-subject-error-positional:
Error shown in place of the {{#create_subject}} button when it is called with an argument that has no name. Parameters:
* $1 - the offending argument
sws-create-subject-error-unknown-arg:
Error shown in place of the {{#create_subject}} button when it receives an unrecognized named argument. Parameters:
* $1 - the offending argument name
sws-create-subject-error-unknown-schema:
Error shown in place of the {{#create_subject}} button when the Schema it names does not exist. Parameters:
* $1 - the Schema name that was asked for
sws-create-subject-error-invalid-page:
Error shown in place of the {{#create_subject}} button when the page it names cannot be a page of this wiki: a malformed title, an interwiki link, or a special page. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title that was asked for
sws-create-subject-error-uncreatable-pag:
Error shown in place of the {{#create_subject}} button on a page-first wiki when the page it names does not exist and is outside the main namespace. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title that was asked for

Error shown in place of the {{#create_subject}} button on a subject-first wiki when the page it names does not exist: such a wiki titles every page it creates for a subject by the subject's ID. "page=new" is a parameter value and stays untranslated. Parameters:
* $1 - the page title that was asked for
sws-create-subject-error-dependent-subje:
Error shown in place of the {{#create_subject}} button, and on Special:CreateSubject, when the schema asked for declares its subjects dependent: such subjects are only added from the editor of the subject that points to them, their host subject. Also shown in place of results in the schema field of the subject creator, when the typed text finds such a schema and nothing it can offer. Parameters:
* $1 - the schema name
sws-create-subject-denied: Body of the dialog the {{#create_subject}} button opens for a user who may not create a subject, used when the wiki supplied no reason of its own.
sws-subject-page-immovable: Reason given when moving a page is refused because the page is titled by the ID of a Subject stored on it, which a subject-first wiki keeps as the title. Shown by Special:MovePage and the API under the standard permission error introduction.
sws-special-sws: Title and description of the [[Special:SWS]] page, which creates Subjects and links to the other SWS pages. "SWS" is the extension name and stays untranslated.
sws-sidebar-overview: Label for the link in the SWS section of the sidebar that navigates to [[Special:SWS]].
sws-overview-layouts-description: Description of the card on [[Special:SWS]] that leads to [[Special:Layouts]].
sws-overview-mappings-description: Description of the card on [[Special:SWS]] that leads to [[Special:Mappings]]. A mapping defines how subjects are expressed in a standard ontology, such as EDM or CIDOC-CRM.
sws-overview-graph-stores-description: Description of the card on [[Special:SWS]] that leads to [[Special:GraphStores]]. A graph store is a database, such as Neo4j, that answers the wiki's queries.
sws-overview-configuration:
Label of the link to [[MediaWiki:SWS]] on [[Special:SWS]], the page holding the wiki's SWS settings.
{{Identical|Settings}}
sws-overview-configuration-description: Description of the card on [[Special:SWS]] that leads to [[MediaWiki:SWS]].
sws-overview-schemas-description: Description of the card on [[Special:SWS]] that leads to [[Special:Schemas]]. A schema defines a type of subject, such as Person, and its properties.
sws-overview-first-steps: Note on [[Special:SWS]], below the button for creating a subject, shown while the wiki has no subjects yet. Only users who may create a subject page see it. "Create subject" is the button's label, {{msg-mw|sws-createsubject-button}}.
sws-main-page-text: Wikitext of the Main Page that SWS's Docker setup writes in place of MediaWiki's own ({{msg-mw|mainpagetext}} and {{msg-mw|mainpagedocfooter}}) when it installs a wiki. {{#create_subject: page=new}} renders the button the text refers to, labelled {{msg-mw|sws-create-subject-default-label}}. Keep the wiki markup, {{#create_subject: page=new}}, the page names and the URLs unchanged; translate the link labels and the headings.
sws-derived-missing: Status in a schema-bound source field when the source was successfully queried and has no statement for the property. This is distinct from an unavailable source; it is not a field value.
sws-property-datatype: Label introducing the source datatype of a property ID in the schema editor.
sws-property-datatype-invalid: Error preventing a schema save when a new or changed source property cannot be resolved or its datatype is incompatible with the selected SWS field type. $1 gives the field, property ID, and/or datatype.
sws-property-type-source-reset: Notice shown after changing a schema field type removes its external property mapping. The property must be selected again for the new type.
